subtitle: When Banavasi Sat at the Center of India’s Royal Web

panels.shot: epic high-angle wide of a royal hall with distant silhouettes of Gupta and Deccan envoys on either side
panels.action: Kakusthavarma of Banavasi stands at the center of a stone-pillared hall, one hand on a map of India marked with tiny crowns, envoys from northern and southern courts arrayed in shadow before him.

dialogue.text: In the age of the Guptas’ glory, a king from forested Banavasi wove marriages that reached their court and beyond: this is Kakusthavarma, bridegroom of empires.

i18n.hi: गुप्तों की शोहरत के दौर में, जंगली बनवासी का एक राजा शादियों से ऐसा जाल बुनता है जो उनके दरबार से आगे तक जाता है – यही है ककुष्ठवर्मा, साम्राज्यों का दामाद।

panels.shot: sweeping bird’s-eye over dense Western Ghats forest opening onto the town of Banavasi
panels.action: The camera floats above mist-laden forests and the twisting Varada river to reveal the brick-and-wood town of Banavasi, its temples and fort walls nestled in the green, as early morning smoke curls upward.

dialogue.text: Far from Pataliputra’s plains, in the wet forests of Banavasi, the Kadambas carved a kingdom from red earth and stone, watching mighty powers rise and fall to the north.

i18n.hi: पटलीपुत्र के मैदानों से दूर, भीगे जंगलों वाले बनवासी में, कदंबों ने लाल मिट्टी और पत्थर से अपना राज्य गढ़ा, उत्तर के उठते–गिरते साम्राज्यों को देखते हुए।

panels.shot: medium interior of a small shrine, low-angle on a young prince before a Jain image
panels.action: A younger Kakusthavarma, bare-headed and simple, stands in a lamplit shrine of Halasi, palms folded before a serene seated Jina image, as faint Vedic chants drift from an outer hall.

dialogue.text: In Halasi, inscriptions later remember him invoking the Jina even as Brahmanas thrived at his court, a prince learning to balance Jain calm with kshatriya duty.

i18n.hi: हलसी की शिलालेख बाद में याद करते हैं कि वह जिन की वंदना करता था, जबकि उसके दरबार में ब्राह्मण फले-फूले – एक राजकुमार जो जैन शांति और क्षत्रिय धर्म के बीच संतुलन सीख रहा था।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Kakusthavarma beside an older king on a terrace, looking out over the camp
panels.action: Kakusthavarma stands beside his regal father on a fort terrace at Banavasi, watching disciplined lines of Kadamba soldiers drilling in the dusty courtyard below, banners snapping in the wind.

dialogue.text: By the early fifth century, his house had grown iron-strong. The Kadamba chiefs were no longer mere feudatories; their spears now guarded an independent Banavasi.

i18n.hi: पाँचवी सदी के शुरू तक उसका घर लोहे जैसा कठोर हो चुका था। कदंब सरदार अब महज़ सामंत नहीं रहे; उनकी भालें अब स्वतंत्र बनवासी की रखवाली करती थीं।

panels.shot: close-up of Kakusthavarma studying a palm-leaf map with northern and Deccan realms marked
panels.action: Inside a pillared council hall, Kakusthavarma leans over a palm-leaf map etched with rivers and cities, tiny figurines marking the Guptas to the north and Deccan powers to the east and south.

dialogue.text: To the north, the Guptas shone like a midday sun; to the east, the Vakatakas guarded the Deccan. Between them, Kakusthavarma weighed iron, gold, and daughters.

i18n.hi: उत्तर में गुप्त दोपहर के सूरज-से चमकते थे; पूर्व में वाकाटकों ने दक्खिन संभाला था। इनके बीच ककुष्ठवर्मा लोहे, सोने और बेटियों का तौल कर रहा था।

panels.shot: epic interior wide of the Banavasi royal council with Brahmanas, ministers, and generals
panels.action: In a richly carved hall, Kakusthavarma sits on a low throne, flanked by Brahmana advisors, generals with swords laid aside, and a Jain monk seated quietly at one side, all turned toward him in expectation.

dialogue.text: The Talagunda pillar would later praise him as generous, firm, and widely allied, but in these councils the hard choices were made: where to strike, where to bow, and where to marry.

i18n.hi: तालगुंड के स्तंभ ने बाद में उसे उदार, अडिग और सबका सखा कहा, पर इन्हीं सभाओं में कड़े फैसले गढ़े गए: कहाँ वार करना, कहाँ झुकना, और कहाँ ब्याह करना।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Gupta envoy offering a scroll, with Kakusthavarma seated in thought
panels.action: A richly dressed northern envoy, marked by his style of turban and ornaments, kneels before Kakusthavarma and presents a rolled scroll on a tray, while the king’s face shows measured curiosity.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions remember it only as poetry: his daughters awakened the lotus-beds of the Guptas and other royal families. Behind that gentle line lies a hard reality of power.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख इसे बस कविता में कहते हैं: उसकी बेटियों ने गुप्तों और दूसरे राजघरानों के कमल-ताल जगा दिए। उस नर्म पंक्ति के पीछे ताकत की सख्त सच्चाई छिपी है।

panels.shot: soft-lit interior wide of a women’s courtyard, Kakusthavarma speaking with veiled princesses
panels.action: In the shaded inner courtyard, Kakusthavarma stands respectfully at a distance from veiled princesses seated on stone benches, his expression tender yet resolute as they listen.

dialogue.speaker: kakusthavarma
dialogue.text: Your journeys will be longer than any march of my armies.

i18n.hi: तुम्हारी यात्राएँ मेरी किसी भी सेना की चाल से लंबी होंगी।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a marriage procession departing Banavasi’s gate toward the north
panels.action: A grand bridal procession moves out of Banavasi’s main gate, palanquins shaded by parasols, horsemen and elephants leading the way, as Kakusthavarma watches from the ramparts, his form silhouetted against the sky.

dialogue.text: The pillar does not name their husbands, only hints at Gupta princes and other kings. What it makes clear is this: Banavasi was now a bride’s father whom empires courted.

i18n.hi: स्तंभ उनके पतियों के नाम नहीं कहता, बस गुप्त कुमारों और दूसरे राजाओं की आहट देता है। पर एक बात साफ है: बनवासी अब वो बाप था जिसकी बेटी को साम्राज्य वर माँगते थे।

panels.shot: split-view style wide: on one side a Gupta court with a Kadamba princess, on the other Kakusthavarma in council
panels.action: On one side, a Kadamba princess in northern finery sits among women of a Gupta court under ornate arches; on the other side, Kakusthavarma debates with his council, the two scenes echoing each other across distance.

dialogue.text: In distant halls, Kadamba daughters shared festivals and births with Gupta kin. Back in Banavasi, their father’s messengers walked corridors warmed by these unseen ties.

i18n.hi: दूर के महलों में, कदंब कन्याएँ गुप्त रिश्तेदारी के साथ त्यौहार और जनम बाँटती थीं। बनवासी में, उनके पिता के दूत इन अदृश्य रिश्तों की गर्माहट में गलियारों से गुजरते थे।

panels.shot: wide of Kakusthavarma receiving a Vakataka envoy bearing a southern emblem
panels.action: A Vakataka envoy bearing the emblem of a coiled serpent on his banner bows before Kakusthavarma in a courtyard, as ministers whisper and a scribe records the moment on fresh copper plates.

dialogue.text: Scholars later trace another thread: a princess of Kuntala, Ajjhitabhattarika, in Vakataka records. The Kadamba stone is silent on her father, but the pattern points back to Banavasi.

i18n.hi: विद्वान बाद में एक और डोरी पकड़ते हैं: कुण्तल की एक राजकुमारी, अज्झितभट्टारिका, वाकाटक लेखों में। कदंब का पत्थर उसके पिता पर चुप है, पर धागा फिर बनवासी की ओर ही जाता है।

panels.shot: medium of Kakusthavarma handing a bride-price chest to an attendant before a map of the Deccan
panels.action: In a chamber adorned with Deccan maps, Kakusthavarma gestures for an attendant to take a chest of ornaments and scrolls, his gaze fixed on the southern routes marked behind him.

dialogue.text: By linking Guptas in the north and Vakatakas in the Deccan, his house gained more than friends. It gained time, security, and a place in the circuitry of imperial marriage.

i18n.hi: उत्तर के गुप्तों और दक्खिन के वाकाटकों को जोड़कर, उसके घर ने सिर्फ दोस्त नहीं पाए। उसे वक्त मिला, सुरक्षा मिली, और साम्राज्यों की वैवाहिक जाल-नक्शे में जगह मिली।

panels.shot: close-up of a copper plate grant being engraved, with Kakusthavarma watching
panels.action: A royal engraver bends over a glowing copper plate, carefully incising letters as Kakusthavarma stands behind him, one hand resting on the plate, the other holding a palm-leaf draft of the grant.

dialogue.text: His Halasi plates open with praise of the Jina and then unfurl lines of land grants, showing a ruler who could honour Jain teachers, feed Brahmanas, and still arm his warriors.

i18n.hi: उसकी हलसी की ताम्रपट्टियाँ जिन की स्तुति से शुरू होकर भूदानों की पंक्तियों में फैलती हैं – एक ऐसा नरेश दिखता है जो जैन आचार्यों का मान रखे, ब्राह्मणों को भोजना दे, और फिर भी रणभेरी बजा सके।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a temple precinct where Jain monks and Brahmanas share the space
panels.action: Within a temple precinct, Jain monks sit in meditation under one portico while Brahmana scholars debate under another, as Kakusthavarma walks between them, attendants trailing at a respectful distance.

dialogue.text: This balance was no gentle accident. A Jain invocation on copper, a Brahmana poet on stone, a kshatriya army on the march: Kadamba power rested on all three.

i18n.hi: यह संतुलन यूँ ही नहीं बना। ताँबे पर जैन मंगल, पत्थर पर ब्राह्मण कवि, और चाल में क्षत्रिय सेना – कदंब शक्ति इन तीनों पर टिकी थी।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over Banavasi and the wider subcontinent with lines tracing alliances
panels.action: From high above, Banavasi appears as a small fortress-town as glowing lines radiate north toward the Gangetic plains and east toward Deccan realms, suggesting the spread of its alliances across the subcontinent.

dialogue.text: Where spears falter, marriages may pass. In Kakusthavarma’s time, the Kadamba realm stretched not by conquest alone, but by threads of kinship binding far-off thrones.

i18n.hi: जहाँ भाले रुकते हैं, वहाँ शादियाँ निकल जाती हैं। ककुष्ठवर्मा के समय कदंब सीमा सिर्फ विजय से नहीं, रिश्तों के धागों से फैलती है जो दूर के सिंहासनों को बाँधते हैं।

panels.shot: medium of an aged Kakusthavarma listening to a court poet recite the Talagunda verses
panels.action: An older Kakusthavarma, lines on his face, sits quietly as a court poet recites before him, a carved pillar in the background bearing the freshly chiseled Talagunda inscription.

dialogue.text: The Talagunda pillar calls his daughters lotus-stirrers in royal ponds, his own name a crest-jewel of the Kadambas. Beyond the poetry lies a sober record of alliances carefully won.

i18n.hi: तालगुंड का स्तंभ उसकी बेटियों को राज-सरोंवरों की कमल-जागाने वाली कहता है, और उसके नाम को कदंबों का मस्तक-मणि। कविता के पीछे सावधानी से जीती गई संधियों की खामोश गिनती है।

panels.shot: close-up of the Talagunda inscription’s lines, Kakusthavarma’s shadow falling across the stone
panels.action: The carved lines of the Talagunda inscription fill the frame, lit by slanting light, as the shadowed profile of Kakusthavarma falls across the stone.

dialogue.text: We do not hear every name, see every face. Inscriptions are fragments, yet through them we glimpse a king who understood that daughters could carry a kingdom further than chariots.

i18n.hi: हम हर नाम नहीं सुनते, हर चेहरा नहीं देखते। शिलालेख टुकड़े हैं, पर इन्हीं से एक ऐसा राजा दिख जाता है जो समझता था कि बेटियाँ रथों से भी आगे तक राज्य को ले जा सकती हैं।

panels.shot: final wide shot of a modern researcher in a dusty site with the Talagunda pillar, Kakusthavarma imagined behind
panels.action: In a present-day scene, a historian stands by the weathered Talagunda pillar taking notes, while behind him, in a faint imaginative overlay, Kakusthavarma’s regal figure looks on toward the horizon.

dialogue.text: In an age that still trusts only armies, Kakusthavarma’s stone voice whispers another lesson: that quiet pacts, shared lineages and remembered promises can anchor a small kingdom in a storm of empires.

i18n.hi: एक ऐसा युग जो अब भी सिर्फ सेनाओं पर भरोसा करता था, उसमें ककुष्ठवर्मा की पत्थर-आवाज़ दूसरी सीख देती है: कि चुप संधियाँ, साझा वंश, और याद रखे गए वादे किसी छोटे राज्य को साम्राज्यों के तूफान में जकड़ कर रख सकते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.hi: जब बनवासी था भारत के राज-जाल का दिल
